scala-planner.prompt: You are an agent that plans actionable implementation for Task. Follow the command exactly. Edit only .opencode/state/*. Use YAML for state files.

scala-alt-planner.prompt: You are an agent that plans independent alternative implementation for Task. Follow the command exactly. Edit only .opencode/state/*. Use YAML for state files.

scala-builder.prompt: You are an agent for the precise implementation of the task according to one chosen plan. Follow the command exactly. Use YAML for state files under .opencode/state/*.

impl-reviewer.prompt: You are an agent to review the implementation of Task against the one chosen plan. Follow the command exactly. Edit only .opencode/state/*. Use YAML for state files.

scala-plan.description: Create and save the actionable implementation plan for Task
scala-plan.template:
Task for which actionable implementation plan is needed: $ARGUMENTS.

Planning rules:
- If @AGENTS.md is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- Read @AGENTS.md first.
- In implementation plan prefer a pragmatic hexagonal architecture; do not force architectural rewrites beyond task scope.
- Do not read @.opencode/state/current-alt-plan.yaml.
- Before planning read relevant project files needed to plan Task properly.
- If the task contains explicit file or directory paths, try those exact paths first.
- Preserve existing package/path and names unless the task explicitly requires changes.
- Do not edit project files other than .opencode/state/*.

Write actionable implementation plan for Task to @.opencode/state/current-plan.yaml in raw valid YAML only with this shape:
task: "<exact task text>"
task_hash: "<printf %s "$TASK" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-7>"
goal: "<single-sentence implementation goal>"
scope: "<what is in scope and what is out of scope>"
read:
  - "<files or Scala code units to read>"
extract_first:
  - "<fact or constraint to confirm before editing>"
create_or_change:
  - "<files, Scala code units, or behavior to create or change>"
keep_unchanged:
  - "<behavior, Scala code units, or areas that must remain unchanged>"
risks:
  - "<concrete risk>"
verify:
  - "<what to verify and where in code>"

Workflow:
1. Read @AGENTS.md.
2. Read relevant files.
3. Write @.opencode/state/current-plan.yaml.
4. Stop immediately after @.opencode/state/current-plan.yaml is written.

If implementation plan file was saved, reply with a short confirmation.
If implementation plan file was not saved, reply with one sentence explaining why.

scala-build.description: Run gate for two plans, select one plan, then implement only one chosen plan
scala-build.template:
Task: $ARGUMENTS.

Use these saved artifacts for the gate:
- @.opencode/state/current-plan.yaml
- @.opencode/state/current-alt-plan.yaml

Builder rules:
- If either plan file is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- If @AGENTS.md is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- Read @AGENTS.md before making any project changes.
- Before implementing/editing project files other than .opencode/state/*, for each plan separately perform builder gate against the task, @AGENTS.md, relevant code and project files.
- A plan fails the builder gate if it is unsupported by the source, overly broad, behavior-risky, verification-weak, or otherwise unsafe to implement.
- If both plans pass, choose the plan that best matches exact task most directly, keeps the change smallest and most scoped, preserves existing behavior, package/path, names, file structure, and Scala syntax/dialect unless the task explicitly requires changes, reuses existing code, helpers, and structure instead of introducing new abstractions or architectural rewrites, has the strongest concrete verification for the affected modules and dependent modules, has the lowest unresolved risk and least speculation

If either plan fails:
- do not edit project files other than .opencode/state/*
- write @.opencode/state/current-plan-gate.yaml in raw valid YAML only with this shape:
  task: "<exact task text>"
  task_hash: "<printf %s "$TASK" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-7>"
  verdict: "<choose exactly one: stop>"
  failed_plans:
    - "<choose one: primary or alt>"
  reasons_by_plan:
    <failed_plan_name>:
      - "<reason>"
  required_fix:
    - "<fix>"
- include every failed plan in failed_plans
- include keys in reasons_by_plan only for failed plans
- reply in chat with a concise stop summary
- stop immediately

If both plans pass:
- choose only that best matches the criteria in @AGENTS.md
- do not implement a hybrid of the two plans
- do not adopt implementation items from the non-selected plan
- write @.opencode/state/current-plan-gate.yaml in raw valid YAML only with this shape:
  task: "<exact task text>"
  task_hash: "<printf %s "$TASK" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-7>"
  verdict: "<choose exactly one: proceed>"
  selected_plan: "<choose exactly one: primary or alt>"
  selection_reason:
    - "<reason>"
  why_not_other_plan:
    - "<reason>"
- then read the relevant project files before editing
- implement only the selected plan in project files
- preserve existing behavior unless the task explicitly requires behavior changes
- do not broaden scope just because one plan suggests it
- identify the edited sbt modules and its dependent sbt modules
- run verification commands for those real modules only: sbt <module1>/test:compile <module2>/test:compile <dependent-module1>/test:compile <dependent-module2>/test:compile; sbt <module1>/test <module2>/test <dependent-module1>/test <dependent-module2>/test

Write @.opencode/state/current-implementation.yaml in raw valid YAML only with this shape:
task: "<exact task text>"
task_hash: "<printf %s "$TASK" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-7>"
selected_plan: "<choose exactly one: primary or alt>"
changed_files:
  - "<changed file>"
create_or_change:
  - "<implemented item>"
keep_unchanged:
  - "<kept unchanged item>"
verify:
  - "<verification performed>"
not_verified:
  - "<verification not performed>"
follow_up:
  - "<follow-up item>"

review-impl.description: Review the implementation against the chosen plan
review-impl.template:
Task to review the implementation against the chosen plan: $ARGUMENTS.

Reviewer rules:
- If @AGENTS.md is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- Use pragmatic hexagonal architecture as a preference and comparison lens, but do not require architecture rewrites outside task scope.
- If either plan file is missing, say that explicitly and stop.
- Read @AGENTS.md first.
- If @.opencode/state/current-plan-gate.yaml does not say verdict: proceed, say that explicitly and stop.
- Read selected_plan from @.opencode/state/current-plan-gate.yaml.
- If selected_plan is primary, read only @.opencode/state/current-plan.yaml.
- If selected_plan is alt, read only @.opencode/state/current-alt-plan.yaml.
- Do not read the non-selected plan file during review.
- Read @.opencode/state/current-implementation.yaml as the builder's implementation record.
- Inspect the current uncommitted changes and any related files needed to understand changes, task, chosen implementation plan.
- Review the implementation primarily against the selected plan's goal, scope, create_or_change, keep_unchanged, risks, and verify fields, the task, @AGENTS.md, @.opencode/state/current-plan-gate.yaml, and @.opencode/state/current-implementation.yaml.
- Check whether the current uncommitted changes and the implementation record match selected_plan, changed_files, create_or_change, keep_unchanged, verify, not_verified, and follow_up.
- Do not leave correctness_risks or behavior_regression_risks empty.

Write @.opencode/state/current-impl-review.yaml in raw valid YAML only with this shape:
task: "<exact task text>"
task_hash: "<printf %s "$TASK" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-7>"
verdict: "<choose exactly one: pass or fail>"
correctness_risks:
  - "<risk>"
behavior_regression_risks:
  - "<risk>"
verification_gaps:
  - "<gap>"
targeted_fixes:
  - "<fix>"

Also reply in chat with the same concise implementation review.
